SSDs are at their core, still a very young technology. You've still got to be careful about the brand you buy, the technology involved. Hard Drives fail, certainly, but I see prematurely dead SSDs at a greater ratio than I see prematurely dead harddrives.
When an SSD truly fails you would be considered lucky to be able to recover any data. While a HDD failure can be recoverable so long as the platters themselves are in fair condition.

I own a IT company for my day job and getting ANYTHING off a ssd that has failed is really a crap shoot. There is little to no chance and the software to do it with a higher chance of success is expesnsive.

There is no industry standard so every controller has it's own way of arranging data on the flash chips. When I had customers with failed SSDs the answer was basically "Sorry, the data is gone forever".
